candidats.description: Original caption: 53-1239 - San Marcos Bridge - April 5, 1952. Screeding concrete with vibrating screed. This screed is not very effective for vibrating except for near the surface. For adequate vibration it was found necessary to supplement with conventional vibrators. As a screed the vibrating screed works well. Note operator at right with conventional vibrator. 53-1240 - San Marcos Bridge - May 7, 1952. Screeding and spreading low slump concrete on deck. State: El Salvador. Place: San Marcos Bridge.

candidats.description: Seabees assigned to Naval Mobile Construction Battalion (NMCB) 4 assemble a power screed in Camp Shields, Okinawa, Japan, on July 30, 2025. NMCB 4 is forward deployed throughout the Indo-Pacific region to support and maintain a free and open Indo-Pacific. As the stand-in, crisis response, naval engineering force, NMCB 4 maintains a ready posture to deliver in-theater expeditionary logistics via expeditionary shore infrastructure, forward damage repair, and mobile construction. (US Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Dakota Rayburn)

candidats.titre: File:USACE maintains navigation on the Ohio River.jpg
candidats.description: Archie Ball (left) uses his "come-along" to pull concrete into place for the screed to smooth while Josh Tyler vibrates concrete to consolidate it after it has been placed on Sill Shell 6 in the casting yard. SS6 is the last of the flat shells for the tainter gate section of the dam being built across the Ohio River as part of the Olmsted Locks and Dam 17 miles upstream from the confluence of the Mississippi. (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers photo by Jon Fleshman)
